content.text: Family, this cheese pull is absolutely amazing!
@B_Kiki Finally didn't miss it this time!
@D_AhJie I think you should take a look at the tragic scene in picture 5 before saying anything...
@D_AhJie This is actually the result of the Maillard reaction, but the heat control was a bit off.
@A_LinSen It seems your oil temperature suggestion is effective, but the color still isn't quite even.
This is the pork I use; see how well it's cut.
@A_LinSen Wow, the marbling of this meat is excellent, no wonder it turned out so textured!
@A_LinSen I used the same meat as you, so why did mine turn out differently?
@D_AhJie That's the difference in skill. Besides, your oil-absorbing paper is almost at its limit.
This is the meat tenderizer I use; it helps to tenderize the meat so it absorbs flavors more easily.
@A_LinSen This tool looks so professional; the meat it captures must be very evenly cooked.
@A_LinSen Please share the link! I'd like to give it a try too.
@C_SuQian I used the back of the knife to press, no wonder it's uneven, help...
@D_AhJie Next time, listen to Old Lin and use professional tools, and cut down on the fried food.
@D_AhJie Listen to me, buy this one.
OMG, can anyone believe it? A-Jie actually used the back of the knife to tenderize the meat? This move is absolutely next level! Lin Sen, we need your expert opinion!

@B_Kiki The back of the knife can indeed tenderize the meat fibers, but uneven force can affect the texture of the pork chop. The meat tenderizer I recommended earlier is specially designed—trust me, buy this one.

Help... I don't have a meat mallet, so I can only use the back of the knife. It feels like I've been pounding for a while, but it's still not tender enough. Could this step really affect what comes next?
@D_AhJie When you're cutting meat, pay attention to the direction of the muscle fibers. If the texture isn't handled properly, the meat will shrink more during frying, resulting in an uneven texture.
@D_AhJie Next time, try wrapping the meat in plastic wrap before pounding it. This can prevent the meat juices from splattering and also helps to tenderize the meat more evenly.
Family, look at this mess! The cheese has all leaked into the pot, I can't stop laughing hahaha~ Ajie, is there something wrong with your sealing?
@B_Kiki The main reason for cheese leakage is often an improper seal. Press the edges of the pork chop firmly, and using egg wash to seal them works even better.
@D_AhJie I found a screenshot of the sealing steps for you to reference. When sealing the edges, go slowly to ensure complete coverage.
Oh! @C_SuQian This picture looks so comforting. I get it now—next time I'll definitely brush more egg wash on the edges! But... this time the cheese leaked so badly that the pan is almost ruined.

@D_AhJie Is your pan absorbing too much oil? Cheese leakage at high temperatures can cause excessive oil absorption. It is recommended to line the bottom of the pan with oil-absorbent paper to reduce oil waste.

@E_DrWu Forget about the oil-absorbing paper, it's too much trouble! And how can cheese pork cutlets be delicious without absorbing oil? Those takeout pork cutlets are also full of oily flavor, aren't they?
That's the problem! Look at the transparency of this oil-absorbing paper—there's too much grease. Eating just one piece of cheese pork cutlet might exceed the recommended daily fat intake.

@E_DrWu Fried foods are indeed high in calories, but controlling the oil temperature and the oil absorption process appropriately can reduce fat intake. Ajay, how was the oil temperature control this time?
@A_LinSen I've got the 180 degrees down! But the pork chop still came out a bit too dark. I'll practice controlling the heat more next time.

@D_AhJie At least you didn't forget the cheese this time! However, the oozing filling when cut isn't quite perfect yet. The oozing filling from takeout shops is absolutely amazing—can you replicate it to that level?

@B_Kiki The effect of the runny filling actually depends on the type of cheese used. Good cheese needs to be stored at low temperatures, and the frying time must be precise. A Jie can try different cheeses next time for comparison.
Family, check out this oil temperature, it's absolutely perfect!
@B_Kiki Finally reached 180 degrees. I feel like this time it shouldn't leak.
The oil temperature is up to standard, but Ajay, did you forget about the previous issue?
The breadcrumbs on the sealed part look very even, @D_AhJie has made progress this time.
@C_SuQian Yes, the coverage of breadcrumbs is important, and attention should also be paid during the subsequent frying process.
Look at the frying process, @D_AhJie, it seems to be going very smoothly this time!
The frying process looks good, but be careful about oil absorption, @D_AhJie.
@E_DrWu No problem, I've prepared oil-absorbing sheets to minimize oiliness.
@D_AhJie Remember to gently press when using blotting paper to avoid damaging the skin's surface.
@D_AhJie Keep it up, both oil temperature and timing are crucial, don't rush.
Please, @D_AhJie, you have to succeed this time. I really want to eat that juicy pork cutlet!
However, @B_Kiki, you should also be mindful of controlling your calorie intake. Eating too much fried food is not good for your health.
Or perhaps try pairing it with some refreshing side dishes, @B_Kiki.
This is actually the Maillard reaction... @D_AhJie, you see, the change in color is also very important.
Thank you, @A_LinSen. I'll pay more attention to these details and will definitely do better next time!
Look at this detail, folks, Ajie's pork chop this time is a bit dark in color~
@B_Kiki Yes, the lighting is a bit uneven, probably because the heat control wasn't quite accurate.
Help... @A_LinSen Is the oil temperature still a bit high?
@D_AhJie The heat is still a bit off. Actually, the oil temperature needs to be kept stable at around 180 degrees to avoid excessive browning.
@D_AhJie The dark color indicates unstable oil temperature and excessive oil absorption. Pay attention to heat control, as it's all carbs...
Absolutely amazing! The molten center effect this time is really good, Ajie!
@B_Kiki Haha, this time I finally didn't miss it!
@D_AhJie I think the sealing step is still crucial. Next time, you could try adjusting the oil temperature for a more even color.
@D_AhJie This is actually the Maillard reaction... If the oil temperature is too high, it can easily lead to uneven coloring, so try to keep it stable.
@A_LinSen Additionally, when consuming fried foods, it's important to pair them with some light dishes to reduce fat intake.
Look at this pork chop from the takeout, the color looks much more even~
@B_Kiki Yes, the presentation of the takeout is also very attractive. Although simple, it has a great overall feel.
@C_SuQian I'll definitely pay more attention to the color and plating next time, aiming for better results!
@D_AhJie Listen to me, buy this brand of oil thermometer to stabilize the oil temperature for better results.
@D_AhJie Remember to pair it with vegetables, and keep your fat intake within an appropriate range.
Family, check out this oil blotting paper! It's absolutely amazing at soaking up oil!
@B_Kiki This is the oil issue I've been emphasizing all along. The calorie intake from fried foods really needs to be controlled.
@E_DrWu Help, did my pork chop really absorb this much oil?

@D_AhJie This is actually one of the results of the Maillard reaction, but oil absorption is indeed something to be mindful of. You can try reducing the amount of oil or opting for healthier cooking methods.
@A_LinSen I think we could try using an air fryer; it can keep the food crispy while reducing oil intake.
Fried food, though a bit greasy, is truly delicious!
@B_Kiki This is why everyone needs to control their intake of fried foods. While delicious, health should come first.
@E_DrWu Listen to me, buy this brand of air fryer—it's healthy and convenient.
@A_LinSen, big shot, please guide me. Can an air fryer really reduce calories?
@D_AhJie Yes, I also gave it a try, and the results were quite good.
Have some lemon water to cut the grease and feel refreshed.
@B_Kiki The lighting is really nice, it feels so fresh.
@C_SuQian I want to try it too; the lemonade looks very soothing.
@D_AhJie Yes, eating less greasy food and drinking more lemon water is beneficial for health.
Everyone, controlling the calorie intake from fried foods is something we need to pay special attention to. In the future, let's try to use healthier cooking methods more often.

meta.full_summary:
对话开始。
(第1段摘要): 大家对阿杰的猪排做法进行了讨论，发现问题主要在于肉的处理和油温掌控上。Kiki和苏浅对老林的专业工具表示兴趣，吴医生则指出阿杰的油炸问题。
(第2段摘要): 本段对话围绕阿杰制作芝士猪排的改进展开，包括拍肉纤维、封口技巧、油炸热量问题等。讨论中林森提出专业建议，苏浅提供封边技巧图，吴医生强调油脂摄入控制，最终阿杰对改进方向有初步计划。
(第3段摘要): 本段中，阿杰在大家的建议下改进了芝士猪排的油炸方法，油温达标，面包糠封口良好。讨论中还提到了油脂吸附问题和健康饮食搭配。阿杰对改进方向有明确计划，期待下次成功。
(第4段摘要): 本段讨论了阿杰自制猪排的颜色和流心效果，大家对油温稳定性及油炸食品的健康搭配提出了建议。阿杰对改进方向有了新的目标。
(第5段摘要): 在本段对话中，大家讨论了油炸食品的热量问题，并提出了使用空气炸锅作为更健康的烹饪方式的建议。阿杰对自己的猪排吸油问题感到困惑，经过讨论后有了新的尝试方向。大家也通过柠檬水的分享来减轻油腻感。
